title: Assistant Bash host execution: run commands via subprocess.run in a worker thread, not asyncio subprocess APIs, so Windows selector loops work
answers: Assistant Bash tool calls fail with NotImplementedError on Windows when MLflow runs multiple workers or reload
Why does the assistant's shell command tool time out or error only on Windows selector event loop?
How does restricted vs full-access Bash run commands on the host for the assistant?
Where is the assistant Bash tool's 120 second timeout handled?
body:
Path: Assistant Bash tool calls that run on the host (non-sandbox) go through mlflow/assistant/providers/tool_executor.py:_execute_bash_on_host, which handles both full-access shell commands and restricted allowlisted argv commands, with a 120s timeout.
Rule: Do not use asyncio.create_subprocess_shell/exec for host-side command execution; the Windows selector event loop (used by multiworker and reload servers) raises NotImplementedError for them. Instead wrap subprocess.run in asyncio.to_thread, passing shell=full_access, stdout/stderr PIPE, cwd, env, timeout=120, and catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired (not asyncio.TimeoutError) for the timeout message.
Symptom: On Windows with the selector event loop, assistant Bash tool calls failed instead of returning command output, so Codex/Claude UI shell commands did not run.
Constraints: Keeps the existing security split: restricted mode still uses shlex.split into argv with shell=False; only full_access uses shell=True. Applies to host execution only; the sandbox path (_execute_bash_in_sandbox) is separate.
applies: Host-side Assistant Bash execution in mlflow/assistant/providers/tool_executor.py; not the sandbox path.
says: Assistant terminal commands fail to execute on Windows multiworker servers.

search: Host-side assistant Bash execution in mlflow/assistant/providers/tool_executor.py:_execute_bash_on_host must use subprocess.run wrapped in asyncio.to_thread rather than asyncio subprocess APIs. This avoids NotImplementedError on Windows selector event loops during multiworker or reload runs while enforcing a 120-second timeout via subprocess.TimeoutExpired. Applies strictly to non-sandbox host command execution, preserving restricted mode argv splitting with shell=False and full-access execution with shell=True.
